Q: Why does deleting an item from keyboard clipboard history not remove it from paste (Android/iOS)? A:

For iOS, read up on the UIPasteboard and its services. The iOS pasteboard contains multiple entries for different underlying types, e.g. text, images (png), URLs, et cetera.

Without knowing anything about the third party clipboard history software, it is impossible to say what they are doing. I would guess they are relying on the UIPasteboardChanged notification, but that is a random guess on my part.

For fun and education, play around with the UIPasteboard services to get the understanding you need. Good luck!

Q: Does cancelling the client-side stream of a Foundry agent response actually stop the server-side run, or does it keep executing MCP tool call? A:

Yup, it eventually dies, but you'll still pay a tiny bit of ghost tax. No infinite zombie agents though.

Here's exactly what happens under the hood:

  • Socket goes RIP: Since you didn't use background=True, this is a standard synchronous HTTP stream (Server-Sent Events). Cancelling the local asyncio task abruptly drops the TCP connection.

  • The Mid-Tool Blind Spot: If it's in the middle of an MCP web search, the Foundry backend is busy waiting for the tool to return. It isn't actively trying to stream tokens to you, so it doesn't realize you pulled the plug yet.

  • The Broken Pipe: The server only finds out you left after the tool call finishes. The exact second it tries to push the next response.output_text.delta down the pipe, it hits a socket error (broken pipe) and the backend kills the generation flow immediately.

Billing & Quota impact:

  • Paid: Input tokens + the compute/quota for that one in-flight web search.

  • Saved: The rest of the LLM generation. It won't keep running wildly in the background.

How to actually fix it: If you want to brutally kill the tool call mid-flight so you don't pay for the search at all, you must pass background=True. That’s the only way to get a response_id upfront so you can explicitly fire a cancellation request:

Python

# Launch in background to get an ID instantly
response = openai.responses.create(
    stream=True,
    background=True,
    tool_choice="required",
    input="What are the latest updates to Microsoft Foundry?",
    extra_body={"agent_reference": {"name": agent_name, "type": "agent_reference"}},
)

# Now you have a handle to kill it properly on disconnect
openai.responses.cancel(response.id)

Without backgrounding, tbh, you're just waiting for the TCP connection to fail.

Q: How can a turn a dataframe that has a row for each pathogen test into having a row for just each tested individual A:

You've given us the rodent id and desired output column names, but not the pathogen column name or the column that identifies whether the pathogen was present/absent. In future, it is appreciated that a sample dataset is supplied. See How to make a great R reproducible example for more details.

Here are some sample data based on your description where the "pathogen" column contains the pathogen name, and the "present" column denotes positive == 1, negative == 0. Adapt to suit your actual data.

# Representative data with only two pathogen-positive rodents
df <- data.frame(
  sampleID = rep(1:60, each = 18),
  pathogen = LETTERS[1:18],
  present = c(c(1, rep(0, 16), 1), rep(0, 1044), c(1, 1, 1, rep(0, 15)))
)

# Base R option
result <- setNames(aggregate(present ~ sampleID, df, \(x) any(x == 1)), c("sampleID", "pathPresence"))

# tidyverse option, requires the dplyr package to be installed and loaded
library(dplyr)
# summarise() present column and return binary column if sum() > 0
result <- df %>%
  summarise(pathPresence = sum(present) > 0, .by = sampleID)

Q: c# RawPrinterHelper sends data to printer, printer spools and states "printed" but doesnt actually print A:

I have been playing around with printing labels sending TSPL to a thermal label printer and was getting the same issue where it would show as printed in the printer queue, but not actually print. I was able to solve it by adding a new line after the last part of the text that I was sending. I have only tested with strings and not files. Here's a sample of the code that worked for me:

SIZE 3,1.5
GAP 3 mm,0
DIRECTION 0
CLS
AZTEC 10,10,0,7,10,"212-867-5309"
TEXT 200,10,"0",90,16,16,0, "Jenny"
PRINT 1
